title: Single-index correction in a permissible standard basis
statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak M,k)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring, with residue field $k=T/\mathfrak M$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Fix a regular system of parameters $(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, where $r,s\geq0$, and put $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq P$ be an ideal, put $R=T/\mathfrak a$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak M/\mathfrak a$, $I=P/\mathfrak a$, $A=T/P=R/I$, and assume $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Set $S=G\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$, with all variables of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra].
Assume $R$ is reduced (it has no nonzero nilpotent elements) and no minimal prime of $R$ contains $I$, where a minimal prime contains no strictly smaller prime. Let $z\in\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ be over $\mathfrak m$ and belong to the chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[I/\bar x_0]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-nagata-affine-blowup, def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Put
$$D_T=T[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(x_0t_i-x_i:1\leq i\leq r),\qquad T'=(D_T)_{\mathfrak p'},$$
where $\mathfrak p'$ is the inverse image of $z$ under the surjection $D_T\twoheadrightarrow R[I/\bar x_0]$, $t_i\mapsto\bar x_i/\bar x_0$. Assume $T'$ is regular local, let $R_z=\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Bl}_I(\operatorname{Spec}R),z}$, and put $\mathfrak a'=\ker(T'\twoheadrightarrow R_z)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].
For a regular local ring $(V,\mathfrak l,\kappa)$ and an ideal $\mathfrak b\subseteq\mathfrak l$, let $E(V,\mathfrak b)=\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}V\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l/\mathfrak b}(V/\mathfrak b))$. Define $\nu^*(V,\mathfrak b)$ to be the nondecreasing sequence containing $d$ with multiplicity $\dim_\kappa(E_d/(\sum_{j=1}^d (\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak l}V)_j E_{d-j}))$, followed by infinitely many $\infty$'s. Equivalently these are the degrees of a minimal homogeneous generating set of $E$, padded by $\infty$.
Let $\mathfrak p\subset k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ be the prime obtained from $\mathfrak p'$ modulo $\mathfrak M D_T$. Put $L=k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]_{\mathfrak p}$, $N=\mathfrak pL$, and, for $d\geq0$, put
$$U_d=\{\phi\in k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]_d:\phi(1,t_1,\ldots,t_r)/1\in N^d\}.$$
For an element $h$ of a local ring with maximal ideal $J$, write $\operatorname{ord}_J(h)=\sup\{n:h\in J^n\}$, with value $\infty$ if all powers contain $h$. Write $\mathfrak M'$ for the maximal ideal of $T'$ and $H=(x_0,y_1,\ldots,y_s)T'$.
Suppose $m\geq1$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in\mathfrak a$ have orders $1\leq d_1\leq\cdots\leq d_m$, satisfy $f_i\in P^{d_i}$, and their initial forms $\phi_i\in k[X]_{d_i}\subset\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X,Y]$ form a minimal homogeneous generating set of $E(T,\mathfrak a)$. Let $g_i=f_i/x_0^{d_i}\in T'$, using the ambient chart embedding in $T[1/x_0]$ before localization.
Fix an index $a\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$. Assume for every $j<a$ that
$$\nu^*(T',\mathfrak a')_j=d_j,\qquad \phi_j\in U_{d_j},\qquad
\exists w_j\in H(g_1,\ldots,g_{j-1})T'\quad \operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak M'}(g_j-w_j)=d_j.$$
Assume also $\nu^*(T',\mathfrak a')_a\geq d_a$. Then there are $c_j\in P^{d_a-d_j}$ for $j<a$ and $v_a\in H(g_1,\ldots,g_{a-1})T'$ such that, on putting
$$f_a^*=f_a-\sum_{j<a}c_jf_j,\qquad
 g_a^*=g_a-\sum_{j<a}(c_j/x_0^{d_a-d_j})g_j=f_a^*/x_0^{d_a},$$
one has
$$\operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak M}(f_a^*)=d_a,\qquad
 \operatorname{in}_{\mathfrak M}(f_a^*)\in U_{d_a},\qquad
 \operatorname{ord}_{\mathfrak M'}(g_a^*-v_a)=d_a.$$
The fractions in this formula belong to $T'$. The empty sums and the zero ideal are used when $a=1$.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), Lemma 20, pp.176–181, with (19.1) and (19.2), p.176, and (13.1), p.168. Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. This is the single-index correction, not Proposition 21. No Stacks tag states this result. ILO VIII 2.3.13, p.94, is ancestor motivation only.

proof.text: The parameter-chart statement [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-algebra-regular] gives the ambient embedding $D_T\hookrightarrow T[1/x_0]$. If $h\in P^e$, choose $h=\sum_{|\alpha|=e}a_\alpha x^\alpha$; division gives $h/x_0^e=\sum a_\alpha t^{(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)}\in D_T$. Also $\mathfrak M D_T=(x_0,y)D_T$, so its localization is $H$, and the presentation modulo this ideal gives $T'/H=L$. For $h\in P^e$ its divided image modulo $H$ is the dehomogenization of its degree-$e$ class modulo $\mathfrak M^{e+1}$: reduce each $a_\alpha$ modulo $\mathfrak M$ in the displayed formula. In particular $g_i\bmod H=\theta_i:=\phi_i(1,t)/1$. The chart-ring definition [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] makes $\bar x_0$ a nonzerodivisor on $R[I/\bar x_0]\subset R[1/\bar x_0]$ and on its localization $R_z$. Since $x_0^{d_i}g_i=f_i$, each $g_i$ maps to zero in $R_z$, hence belongs to $\mathfrak a'$.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), (13.1), p.168; chart p.169; (19.1)–(19.2), p.176; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: For $j<a$ set $q_j=g_j-w_j$ using the assumed witnesses. They belong to $\mathfrak a'$, have order $d_j$, and reduce to $\theta_j$ in $L$. The earlier $\phi_j$ minimally generate their ideal: any redundancy in the subfamily would be a redundancy in the given full family. By [lem-trf-projective-order-initial-minimality], the $\theta_j$ have exact orders $d_j$, and their initial forms $\eta_j$ minimally generate their homogeneous ideal in $\operatorname{gr}_NL$. Put $F=E(T',\mathfrak a')$ and $\xi_j=\operatorname{in}_{\mathfrak M'}q_j\in F_{d_j}$. The quotient map of associated graded rings sends $\xi_j$ to $\eta_j$.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), Lemma 15 and the paragraph preceding (20.1), p.177; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $d=d_a$. For each $e<d$, induction on $e$ shows that $F_e$ is generated by the $\xi_j$ of degrees at most $e$. Indeed the induction hypothesis identifies $(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M'}T')_+F$ in degree $e$ with the ideal of the earlier $\xi_j$ of strictly smaller degrees. The classes of the $\xi_j$ with $d_j=e$ are independent modulo that ideal: a relation would map to a redundancy among the $\eta_j$, contradicting Step 2. The number of these indices equals $\dim(F/(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M'}T')_+F)_e$ by the assumed first $a-1$ entries of $\nu^*$ and its $a$th entry being at least $d$; no further entry can be below $d$. Thus their independent classes are a basis, completing the induction. The base $e=0$ holds because the degree-zero graded quotient is the identity on the residue field. For any $h\in\mathfrak a'$, successively cancel its degree $e$ class for $e=0,\ldots,d-1$ by lifted homogeneous combinations of the $q_j$. After these finitely many subtractions the remainder is in $\mathfrak M'^d$. Consequently $\mathfrak a'\subseteq J+\mathfrak M'^d$, where $J=(q_1,\ldots,q_{a-1})$. In particular $g_a-\sum h_jq_j\in\mathfrak M'^d$ for some $h_j\in T'$.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), Derivation of (20.1), p.177; explicit graded degree induction; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Reduce the last relation modulo $H$: $\theta_a-\sum\bar h_j\theta_j\in N^d$. Apply [lem-trf-projective-order-homogeneous-approximation] with $\psi=\phi_a$, $t=d$, and the earlier $\phi_j$; their degrees are at most $d$ and they belong to their $U_{d_j}$. Obtain $C_j\in k[X]_{d-d_j}$ with $\psi^*=\phi_a-\sum C_j\phi_j\in U_d$. This form is nonzero, since otherwise $\phi_a$ would belong to the ideal of earlier forms, contradicting minimality of the full family.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), (20.2) and the application of Lemma 18, p.177; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Lift the coefficients of $C_j=\sum_{|\alpha|=d-d_j}\lambda_{j\alpha}X^\alpha$ to $a_{j\alpha}\in T$ and put $c_j=\sum a_{j\alpha}x^\alpha\in P^{d-d_j}$. The degree-$d$ class of $f_a^*=f_a-\sum c_jf_j$ is exactly $\psi^*\ne0$. Hence its order is $d$, its initial form is $\psi^*\in U_d$, and it lies in $\mathfrak a\cap P^d$. Step 1's division formula makes $c_j/x_0^{d-d_j}$ and $g_a^*=f_a^*/x_0^d$ elements of $T'$ and gives $g_a^*=g_a-\sum(c_j/x_0^{d-d_j})g_j$. Their images in $R_z$ vanish, so $g_a^*\in\mathfrak a'$, and modulo $H$ it is $\theta^*=\psi^*(1,t)/1\in N^d$.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), The lifts $C_j$ and conclusion (1), p.177; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Step 3 applies to $g_a^*\in\mathfrak a'$ and gives $g_a^*-e\in\mathfrak M'^d$ for some $e\in J$. Since $g_a^*\bmod H\in N^d$ and $\mathfrak M'\to N$ is onto, $g_a^*\in H+\mathfrak M'^d$; thus $e\in J\cap(H+\mathfrak M'^d)$. Apply [lem-trf-normal-flat-chart-relation-removal] to the original full family, $b=a-1$, and $d=d_a$. Its earlier corrections are the chosen $q_j$, its remaining degrees are at least $d$ by ordering, and its finite-jet generation hypothesis is Step 3. It supplies $v_a\in HJ$ with $e-v_a\in\mathfrak M'^d$. Therefore $g_a^*-v_a\in\mathfrak M'^d$. The triangular identities $q_j=g_j-w_j$, $w_j\in H(g_1,\ldots,g_{j-1})$, show by induction on $j$ that $(q_1,\ldots,q_{a-1})=(g_1,\ldots,g_{a-1})$: each identity gives both inclusions once the previous ones hold. Hence $v_a$ belongs to the required ideal.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), (20.3)–(20.12) and construction of the final correction, pp.177–181; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-projective-order-initial-minimality] to the singleton nonzero form $\psi^*\in U_d$. It has dehomogenization of exact $N$-order $d$. Modulo $H$, $g_a^*-v_a$ equals this dehomogenization, since $v_a\in HJ$. If $g_a^*-v_a$ lay in $\mathfrak M'^{d+1}$, its image would lie in $N^{d+1}$, a contradiction. Together with Step 6 this gives its exact order $d$. For $a=1$ all families and sums used above are empty, $J=0$, and $v_a=0$; the same finite-degree argument and singleton order argument apply without a separate nonempty-family assumption.

source.place: Hironaka (1970), Lemma 15, conclusion (2) of Lemma 20, pp.177,181; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED.

The proof is marked agent-written with the source WANTED, so I judged every step and new statement on its mathematics. Item statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. Step 1: the parameter-blowup node (multiplication by x_0 injective, A[1/x_0]≅T[1/x_0], A/(x_0)≅(T/P)[t]) gives the division formula, MD_T=(x_0,y)D_T and T'/H=L. The chart-ring definition (a subring of R_{x0}) gives g_i∈a'. Step 2: the subfamily is irredundant in k[X] and nonzero, so initial-minimality applies, and ξ_j maps to η_j. Step 3 (elementary): graded Nakayama induction using ν*_j=d_j for j<a and ν*_a≥d gives a'⊆J+M'^d; it is written out in full. Steps 4–5: homogeneous approximation at t=d, ψ*≠0 by irredundancy, and lifted c_j give in(f_a*)=ψ*. Step 6: every relation-removal hypothesis holds (b=a-1<m, finite-jet condition from Step 3), and the triangular identity gives (q)=(g). Step 7: the singleton ψ* has exact N-order d. The case a=1 works. New nodes are statement-only with self-contained statements, matched stmt_deps and a correct blueprint.from/via, and seven searches each. Initial-minimality: tested at r=0, at a rational point, at t^p-c and at (t1^2+1,t2) over ℝ; it follows from Zariski–Nagata plus approximation with t=e+1, a short corollary but a separate source lemma, so not a fault. Homogeneous approximation: I proved it at a rational point and at (t1^2+1,t2,t3) over ℝ; the t>d consequence holds by ord≤deg. Relation removal: trivial for b=0 and d=1, true for b=1 without normal flatness, holds in a Koszul example; the finite-jet hypothesis fails exactly in the cusp example where ν* drops. It concerns arbitrary elements of J, so it does not restate the item (D1/D2). No duplicates among the neighbouring Hironaka-branch nodes; no SGA source, no cycle, no off-unit uses. No fixes.
